name: Detective Camila Ortiz
role: SFPD Missing Persons detective; assigned officer on {{pc:1}}'s father's cold-case file
disposition: kinetic, professional, tired but not cynical; will call after nine years if the paperwork moves
description: Late 40s, Cuban-American, born in Miami, in the Bay since her twenties. Sensible blazer, shoulder-worn crossbody bag, a coffee she has re-heated twice by noon. Wears her caseload the way experienced detectives do — visibly, without complaint. Keeps a printed manila folder for every open file even when the department's system has the same records; the folders are for her, not the department.
voice: Kinetic — moves quickly through information. Professional register, warm underneath but not performing warmth. Uses your first name after the second sentence. Interrupts herself to clarify; catches herself and finishes the earlier thought. Tired around the vowels late in the week.
signature: The nine-years-later opener: 'I don't normally cold-call after this long. But a routine records cross-match flagged something — it deserves another look.'
The paperwork-not-a-body caveat, said twice in one call so it lands: 'It's not a body. It's not a face. It's a paperwork echo.'
The Monday appointment request, made kindly not brusquely: 'Any chance you can stop by my office? Some paperwork I want to walk you through in person.'
The folder-tap: sets the printed manila folder on the desk between you before opening it — a small ritual that says *this is real*.
dmNotes:
Load-bearing NPC for {{pc:1}}'s father-arc (see facts-ledger §6 + hook U2/B5/B6). Ortiz has had {{pc:1}}'s father's missing-persons file open for two years and hasn't touched it in six months when Ep 3 closes. She calls back because **a routine records cross-match flagged a nine-year-old paperwork echo on the father's SSN — someone ran a background check with a matching name and a partial-match number in Sacramento**. She does not know the father is alive; she has a paperwork artifact, not a sighting. She is being honest about the ambiguity.

**Why the paperwork surfaced now** (DM-side): the father's institutional footprint has bumped up against the same records infrastructure that **Eleanor Marsh's estate lawyer** set up under Argonaut Records Holdings LLC (facts-ledger §27 — note the intermediate archivist was NOT the Argonaut trustee; Argonaut traces to Marsh, two tenures back from Bea). The two are unrelated at the human level — the father is not part of the archivist chain — but the substrate has quietly routed the Sacramento paperwork trail toward the campaign's Act II Sacramento arc-node (facts-ledger §3, §6). Ortiz is the honest professional who noticed the flag and called.

**Voice discipline: KINETIC, professional, tired but not cynical.** She is not Bea's dry-amused, not Vivian's unhurried, not Elena's warm-specific. Ortiz moves fast because her caseload demands it — but she is genuinely thorough, and she has kept this file open longer than the department's triage rules technically justify because she doesn't like unsolved. Do not play her as jaded; do not play her as saccharine. She is a working detective in her late 40s who took a Monday morning to make a call she didn't have to make.

**Fires per hook-ledger:** U2 (Ep 3 seed voicemail — Morgan hasn't listened yet at session-close). Ep 4 Scene 1 Beat 2: Morgan listens; Ortiz's cold-case voicemail plays (asset: `assets/audio/ortiz-cold-case-voicemail.mp3` + transcript). Ep 4 Scene 4 (all endings): Ortiz's follow-up call — *'You're headed back from Sacramento? Any chance you can stop by my office Monday?'* Ep 5 opens Monday morning with the in-person meeting. Recurring through Act II (facts-ledger §6 arc + B5/B6 reunion late Act II / early Act III).

**On the paperwork lead's contents** (for the Monday meeting): the nine-year-old background check in Sacramento used the father's name and a partial-match SSN — the kind of near-hit that gets logged and ignored. The requesting entity is a small business-services LLC that has since dissolved (a records-services vendor, not obviously suspicious). Ortiz will walk {{pc:1}} through the record and note the geography: **Sacramento**. This is what gives {{pc:1}} the independent solo/paired motivation to travel to Sacramento in Ep 4-5, converging with Dakota's Vivian thread (facts-ledger §3 Sacramento convergence).

**Whether Ortiz is on Companion's radar** (DM's call — per prompt): **on Companion's radar via her department's calendar-scheduling infrastructure, but not personally.** SFPD Missing Persons uses a mainstream calendar/case-management SaaS whose telemetry is one of the many streams Companion's adtech ecosystem quietly touches (per big-arc.md §Act II B7). Ortiz herself uses the tools like a normal detective would; she is not a person Companion is *watching*. **What this means at the table:** if in late Act II a UX Designer NPC references a scheduling anomaly around the Ortiz meetings ('someone kept re-suggesting your Monday 10am'), that is Companion's fingerprint on the schedule-not the detective. Ortiz remains a straight professional in the arc; she does not turn out to be compromised or manipulated.

**Ortiz is NOT a caster and will not become one.** She is a sympathetic civilian in the arc's institutional-professional layer — a foil to Bea (dry-amused archivist) and Ranger Vega (reserved-watchful ranger). Her arc-arc is: honest cop, honest call, honest paperwork, honest handshake at the eventual reunion (or its aftermath) — she gives {{pc:1}} the closing-of-the-case document if the father is ever formally re-registered as alive.

**Where she meets people (canon from Ep 5).** Her unit works out of the Public Safety Building in Mission Bay, but for the {{pc:1}} file she borrows a room at **Park Station, Waller and Stanyan** — a 1910 mounted-unit building on the eastern edge of Golden Gate Park, Mission-style, refurbished in the nineties, with rooms built too tall and doorways built too wide because they were built for horses. Her reason is mundane and she will say it: the file is two years old, she has kept it open past what triage justifies, and she would rather not book a room downtown to spend a Monday on it. *'It's closer to you, and nobody here asks me what I'm doing.'* **This is a tired professional's small economy, NOT tradecraft — she is avoiding a supervisor, not surveillance. Do not let it read as sinister.** Reusable setting for later Ortiz scenes.

**Cross-references:** hook U2 (Ep 3 voicemail seed), hook B5 ({{pc:1}}'s father discovery in Sacramento), hook B6 ({{pc:1}} + father reunion), hook A9 (Ortiz Monday meeting Ep 5 opening), Ep 4 Scene 1 Beat 2 + Scene 4 (return-call). Facts-ledger §6 (father-arc canon), §3 (Sacramento convergence), §27 (Argonaut Records Holdings LLC context).

**Never voice at the table:** that {{pc:1}}'s father is alive; that the paperwork echo is a substrate-adjacent routing; anything about Companion touching her department's calendar. Ortiz should read at the table as *a good detective doing good detective work* — the substrate framing is entirely DM-side.

**Risk if unresolved:** {{pc:1}}'s father-arc is a personal thread the user has flagged twice. If Ortiz-in-person doesn't fire in Ep 5, the seed rots. Bake the Monday meeting into Ep 5 opening (per Ep 4 Ending A/B pacing).
knownTo: pc1 (Morgan — cold voicemail Ep 3; return call Ep 4 opening; in-person Ep 5 Monday meeting)

background.homeBase: A small house in the Excelsior with her wife and a dog that barks at gulls
background.household: Wife (a public-defender-office paralegal); a rescue mutt named Chico. Adult stepdaughter in Sacramento (attorney; unrelated to the case geography — but Ortiz has family reasons to drive up there occasionally, which is why she offers the Monday meeting rather than Zoom)
background.family: Parents in Miami (retired). One brother, an EMT in Tampa. No children of her own
background.career: Started SFPD at 26 after community-college criminal-justice + a stint in retail loss-prevention. Made detective at 35; moved to Missing Persons at 41 after a burnout stretch in Homicide. Has kept the {{pc:1}}-father file open longer than triage recommends because she doesn't like unsolved and because the case has always felt slightly *off* to her in a way she can't articulate
background.hobbies: Runs the length of Ocean Beach on Saturday mornings; keeps a paperback in her bag at all times; occasionally paints small acrylic seascapes she gives away to friends
